- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.5–2% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.3 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.2 to 0.5), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values or use sentiment-weighted moving average.
